note: Third-party work the workbench cannot run without. This file is edited by a person: it is
a STATEMENT about dependencies, not a copy of them. release.py builds the release by it, and
writes THIRD-PARTY.md by it as well - the list of third-party work inside the package with
its licences, which the GPL-3 obliges us to show.
The release is self-contained: everything that can go inside is inside. There is
nothing for the user to download separately. A dependency that cannot go inside is
marked bundle: false, and then its entry has to say where to get it.
name      what it is called, for a person
kind      runtime | python-package | folder - what the thing is
why       what the workbench needs it for; an entry without this field must not be added
required  false - everything works without it except what why names
bundle    whether it goes inside the release; the LICENCE decides that, not convenience
into      where inside the package it goes
setting   the morphbench.json key that sets the path by hand when something is off
proof     files inside the folder it is identified by - so someone else's is not taken
search    where to look for it on the builder's machine; * as in file names, %VARIABLE% from the environment
source    where it was taken from and where its sources lie - the GPL asks for this when a binary is handed out
license   what it is distributed under

dependencies.name: Python
dependencies.why: the whole workbench is written in it

dependencies.name: numpy
dependencies.why: all the arithmetic over vertices: morphs, strain, bounds, capsules

dependencies.name: pillow
dependencies.why: writing frames to PNG (render, sheet); everything else works without it, the page included

dependencies.name: PyNifly
dependencies.why: reading and writing NIF and the TRI/TRIP morph files, and reading the Havok packfile container skeleton.hkx is kept in; the workbench has no parsers of its own for these formats and must not have any - a second reading of a format is one that can drift away from the first. Of skeleton.hkx it decodes on top only the three classes PyNifly does not: the skeleton, the mapper and the ragdoll instance

remark: Blender itself is NOT needed: the workbench never touches bpy, only the add-on folder.
Only the parts named in keep travel: the workbench imports `pyn`
(with NiflyDLL.dll beside it) and loads only
tri/trifile.py and tri/tripfile.py directly. The Blender nif/ and tri UI modules,
assets, hkxcmd.exe and the material list are never used and do not ship.
keep is an allow-list on purpose: a future release of the add-on can add another
folder, and a deny-list would let it in without anyone noticing.
That folder usually sits among the Blender add-ons - which is where the build looks.
Putting it inside the package is lawful: the licences match. NiflyDLL.dll is a binary, so
the GPL requires naming where its sources came from - see source and THIRD-PARTY.md.
The add-on has no Nexus page for Skyrim; its home is GitHub, and there is one more page
